tasks.short: Plan and conduct industrial ecology field research

steps.what: Plan field research by defining questions, methods, sites and representative observation conditions
Conduct field research, observe industrial and ecological conditions and resolve emerging evidence gaps

tasks.design: Retain field research design and physical investigation with the ecologist, recording the plan in {DOCS} and observations in the {OTHER} field research environment. The ecologist adapts enquiry to actual industrial and ecological conditions rather than treating a standard form as a sufficient research method.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful field evidence depends on observing the right conditions and recognising unexpected mechanisms.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital collection tools support records, but this digest does not establish a saving in scientific planning or field observation.
tasks.still_hard: A convenient site or observation period may not represent the system the research aims to explain.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist recognises missing context and changes the investigation to test the explanation.
tasks.altitude: Fieldwork effort and research responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify practical limits of the proposed observations

evidence.claim: Retaining scientific field planning and physical investigation is a model-knowledge boundary; data platforms do not establish replacement of those activities.

assumptions: Boundary is the ecologist's field plan and investigation, not other researchers' labour or later model development.

Site staff provide existing constraints and evidence. The ecologist captures questions, methods and observation scope in fully retained s1; field observations are produced during s2 rather than assumed ready beforehand.
No structured representative-site or sufficient-evidence flag is presumed. Missing observations lead to manual enquiry or further field activity within retained work.
Test existing field-record functions before custom code. OTHER denotes field research recording and instrument software.
No new automation or capture obligation is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; existing instrument runtime earns no labour saving.
research_questions: Which field observations would challenge the current explanation of the industrial-ecological system?

already_counted.description: Scientific planning and physical field investigation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with zero added upkeep. Research planning and physical observations retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create ecological mathematical models with checked implementation drafts

steps.what: Define the ecological model's equations, assumptions, parameters, boundary conditions and validation tests
Create complex dynamic model implementations from the specified equations and tests

loop.purpose: Draft numerical implementation of an ecologist-specified model
loop.input: equations, assumptions, units, boundary conditions and validation specification
loop.output: implementation draft with traceable equation mappings and test results
loop.check: Ecologist inspects equation meaning, units, conservation or limiting behaviour, numerical stability and agreement with independent reference calculations
loop.stop: One implementation and one correction; failed tests or unclear scientific mappings return to manual implementation
loop.why_not_simpler: A configurable solver may not directly represent a novel coupled ecological model; use native equation configuration first where it can

steps.what: Validate scientific behaviour and accept the exact mathematical model version for research use

tasks.design: First test native equation and solver configuration in the {OTHER} mathematical modelling environment. Where implementation still requires bespoke code, use a bounded draft from the ecologist's specification in {DOCS}, then inspect numerical and scientific behaviour before accepting the exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Implementing specified coupled equations required technical coding effort alongside scientific model design.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded implementation drafting can assist coding while independent tests and scientific inspection remain mandatory parts of the work.
tasks.still_hard: An executable model can implement the wrong mechanism or produce misleading behaviour outside tested conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist chooses the causal structure and knows which observed behaviour would invalidate it.
tasks.altitude: Some implementation effort may fall; model structure and scientific acceptance stay with the ecologist.

reach.task: Check stability and limiting behaviour of coupled ecological equations
reach.learn: Independent numerical validation and sensitivity testing

evidence.claim: Bounded code drafting from explicit ecological equations is a model-knowledge design; this digest provides no measured ecological model implementation result.

assumptions: Boundary is model specification, implementation and research acceptance, not field data collection or forecast batch preparation. Reused implementation is counted once when another task uses the model.

The ecologist produces equations, variable definitions, units, parameter sources, initial conditions and independent validation cases in fully retained s1. No ready scientifically-valid flag or complete model specification is assumed.

The drafting loop starts only after s1. Missing parameters or contradictory equations return to manual scientific work; inspection and implementation corrections remain in s2 and scientific validation in s3.
Test native solver configuration before generating code. OTHER denotes mathematical modelling and numerical analysis software; solver runtime is not saved labour.
The model is accepted for a stated research scope, not certified as universally predictive. Test maintenance and specialist checks have additional upkeep allowances.
unknowns: Model novelty and native solver fit
Actual coding versus scientific design effort
research_questions: Does assisted implementation reduce total effort after independent numerical and scientific checks?

already_counted.description: Inspect implementation meaning and correct failed mappings or tests
Validate behaviour and accept the research model version

incremental.description: Maintain test cases, dependencies and implementation checks
Numerical specialist reviews additional solver ambiguities

approvals.approved_version: Exact implementation version, equations, parameter schema, validation results and stated research scope checked in s3; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=84; gross 16 minus 9 focal upkeep gives central net 7. Range covers models needing full manual implementation and modest coding reuse; scientific specification and final validation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate ecology programmes with repeatable statistical preparation

steps.what: Define programme outcomes and verify data, comparison groups, measurement limits and statistical analysis choices
Prepare specified statistical analyses and comparison displays for industrial ecology programmes
Evaluate effectiveness by checking assumptions, uncertainty and alternative explanations for the observed results

tasks.design: Configure repeatable analyses in the {OTHER} statistical analysis environment from ecologist-checked data and a specified method. Keep assumptions in {DOCS}; the ecologist evaluates effectiveness rather than treating statistical output as proof of programme causation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated analytical preparation consumed time before the ecologist examined whether programme outcomes were attributable to the intervention.
tasks.enabler_now: Native statistical templates can apply a checked specification without selecting the evaluation design.
tasks.still_hard: Selection effects, changing conditions and incomplete outcome measurement can explain apparent improvements.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist distinguishes a measured association from credible evidence of programme effectiveness.
tasks.altitude: Repeated statistical preparation may fall; evaluation design and causal interpretation stay unchanged.

reach.task: Check comparison design and alternative explanations

evidence.claim: Configured statistical preparation from a checked evaluation design is a model-knowledge proposal; the digest provides no measured industrial ecology programme-evaluation saving.

assumptions: Boundary covers evaluation preparation and interpretation, not collecting routine programme data or changing the programme.

Programme staff produce dated observations, intervention records and outcome measurements. In fully retained s1 the ecologist captures record ids, outcome definitions, units, periods, comparison groups, missingness, exclusions and statistical choices.

s2 runs only after s1 produces the dataset and specification. No ready comparable-group or programme-effective flag is presumed; missing definitions and inconsistent records return to manual checking in s1.
Test native statistical configuration before custom code. OTHER denotes statistical analysis software; existing calculation runtime itself earns no saving.
Substantive assumption checks and interpretation retain full time. Analytical upkeep and additional programme-source clarification are explicitly counted.
research_questions: Can configured preparation reproduce checked analyses without hiding exclusions or weakening causal interpretation?

already_counted.description: Capture and verify evaluation data and method choices
Assess effectiveness, assumptions and alternative explanations

incremental.description: Maintain analytical definitions and source mappings
Programme staff clarify changed outcome or intervention records

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 22. Range covers analyses already configured and limited repeated preparation; evaluation design and causal judgement retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Forecast ecosystem conditions using explicit scenario batches

steps.what: Specify forecast scenarios, checked model versions, changing industrial practices and environmental assumptions
Prepare forecast runs and comparative outputs for the specified ecosystem scenarios
Forecast future ecosystem status by interpreting scenario behaviour, model limits and uncertainty

tasks.design: Configure forecast batch preparation in the {OTHER} ecological modelling environment using scenarios and an existing model checked by the ecologist. Keep assumptions and interpretation in {DOCS}; the ecologist assesses forecast credibility and uncertainty without calling a simulated trajectory a known future state.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated scenario setup and output arrangement required manual preparation after scenario assumptions had been chosen.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch configuration can apply explicit parameter sets and arrange comparable outputs.
tasks.still_hard: Future industrial behaviour and ecological responses may differ from both the scenarios and the model structure.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist identifies when a forecast is outside the model's evidential scope and explains uncertainty to planners.
tasks.altitude: Repeated forecast preparation may fall; scenario judgement and future-condition interpretation stay unchanged.

reach.task: Use conditional forecasts without treating scenarios as predictions of certainty

evidence.claim: Configured scenario batch preparation is a model-knowledge design; the digest does not establish ecosystem forecast accuracy or measured labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary starts with an existing research model and covers forecast specification, run preparation and interpretation. Model creation and validation belong to their own workflow and are counted once, including task 16891 where relevant.

In fully retained s1 the ecologist produces model version, scenario id, horizon, parameter values, units, initial conditions, changed practices, output variables and provenance. No ready valid-forecast or likely-future flag is presumed.
s2 starts only after the checked specification exists. Missing parameters, unsupported extrapolation or failed runs return to manual checking; scientific interpretation remains in s3.
Test native batch settings before custom code. OTHER denotes ecological modelling and scenario analysis software. Savings concern manual setup and output arrangement, never solver execution time.
Where batch preparation is already configured there is no new gain. Parameter mapping and scenario-source upkeep have explicit allowances.
unknowns: Existing model scope and independent validation
research_questions: Can native batches remove repeated setup while keeping scenario and model limitations visible?

already_counted.description: Capture checked scenarios and model scope

incremental.description: Maintain batch parameter mappings and failed-run checks
Model or source specialists clarify changed scenario inputs

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross 20 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 12. Range covers already-configured batches and modest repeated-setup gains; scenario judgement and forecast interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some implementation, statistical preparation and forecast setup may fall; field investigation, model structure and scientific interpretation remain with the ecologist.
reach: Check numerical behaviour with modelling specialists
role.ambitious_version: An ecologist who makes computational work reproducible while keeping causal and predictive claims within the evidence.
